note: 0.3.0 added incomplete-recording listing, rescue and deletion so an interrupted capture is visible, recoverable and reclaimable from the Web console; 0.3.1, 0.3.2 and 0.3.3 fix three defects the board run exposed: an over-strict rescue gate that refused a session whose stream held fewer access units than its frame index (now reconciled, index truncated to the published pair count, STREAM_LENGTH_MISMATCH recorded); unreferenced rescue work directories that were invisible and undeletable once the orphan was gone (now listed as staging_leftover); and a deletion idempotency check that treated any completed deletion as a replay and so could not reclaim residue appearing later. Rescue remuxes raw H.265 access units into MP4 with the new stdlib adapter/umi_remux.py, because this image cannot install h265parse and no GStreamer element can produce hvc1 from Annex-B; re-encoding was rejected as it would damage the y8 luma infrared streams. Board evidence: six real orphans listed with correct sizes and pair counts; a 20 s capture completes (600 pairs / 8000 IMU / exit 0); a SIGKILL-induced orphan rescues, publishes as COMPLETE_LOCAL with recovery_hint and an honest DEGRADED quality status, decodes with mppvideodec without error, and deletes through the existing catalog path (ledger DELETED, no later capture blocked); the muxed access-unit count matches the native collector's own frame count exactly (659/659); live data is refused; space verdicts are enforced (32 GB orphan needs 16.72 GiB against 7 GiB free). The operator deleted 46.9 GB of orphans through the new console path and a 3.1 GB work directory was reclaimed, leaving 52.76 GiB free. Rollback: current -> releases/0.2.6 or 0.3.x per DEPLOYMENT_AND_USAGE.zh-CN.md section 9.
